dedupe_keys.name: fcc supply chain information collection on huawei and zte equipment in us networks 2020

description: This collection records which US telecommunications carriers use equipment or services from Huawei and ZTE, and what it would cost to replace them. It was gathered after the Federal Communications Commission's November 2019 order barring Universal Service Fund support for equipment from companies that pose a national security threat, and after Huawei and ZTE were finally designated as such in June 2020. On 4 September 2020 the FCC released a list of eligible telecommunications carriers, or their affiliates and subsidiaries, that reported using at least some Huawei or ZTE equipment or services, and aggregate cost estimates: about 1.837 billion US dollars to remove and replace the equipment across all filers, of which about 1.618 billion for filers that appeared to qualify for reimbursement under the Secure and Trusted Communications Networks Act of 2019. The collection led to the reimbursement programme for removing and replacing such equipment. Coverage: US carriers receiving Universal Service Fund support, 2020. Format and access: FCC public notice and list as PDF, free. Caveats: carriers outside the Fund may be missing; equipment types and locations are not given; costs are self-reported estimates that later rose. Simulation uses: supply chain and security risk in telecom networks, cost of replacing untrusted vendors, and scenarios of forced equipment swaps. Related records: the EU 5G coordinated risk assessment addresses the same vendor risk in Europe.
